import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.2

by V. S. Anashin

A *mixed identity* of a group $G$ is, by definition, an identity of an algebraic system
obtained from $G$ by supplementing its signature by some set of $0$-ary operations.
One can develop a theory of mixed varieties of groups on the basis of this notion
(see, for example, V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*,
Math. USSR Sbornik **57** (1987), 171–182). Construct an example of a class of groups
which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed under taking factor-groups, Cartesian
products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that contain the diagonal subgroup.

Here a mixed identity is a word $w$ in variables from a set $X$ and constant symbols from a
set $C$ (the $0$-ary operations), i.e. an element of the free group on $X \sqcup C$. A group
$G$ with an interpretation $c \colon C \to G$ of the constants satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates
to $1$ for all values of the variables in $G$. A class of groups is a *mixed variety* (in
Anashin's sense) if, for some set $W$ of mixed identities, it consists exactly of the groups
in which all identities of $W$ hold for some interpretation of the constants.

Every mixed variety is closed under isomorphism, factor-groups, Cartesian products (over
arbitrary index sets, so it contains the trivial group) and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup. The problem asks for a class showing that these closure
properties do not characterise mixed varieties, in contrast with Birkhoff's theorem for
ordinary varieties.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
* V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*, Math. USSR Sbornik
  **57** (1987), 171–182.
-/
namespace Kourovka.«10.2»

blocks.docstring:
A group `G` together with an interpretation `c : C → G` of the constant symbols `C`
satisfies the mixed identity `w` (a word in the variables `X` and the constants `C`) if `w`
evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G` for the variables.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `FreeGroup.lift` (used as the evaluation map); no existing 'identity'/'law'/'variety' predicate exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.2».SatisfiesMixedIdentity
justification.why_needed: Mathlib has no notion of a group (with constants) satisfying an identity/law. Defined as: for all assignments `x : X → G` of the variables, `FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c) w = 1`, where `w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)` is a word in variables `X` and constant symbols `C` and `c : C → G` interprets the constants.

blocks.name: SatisfiesMixedIdentity
blocks.text:
/-- A group `G` together with an interpretation `c : C → G` of the constant symbols `C`
satisfies the mixed identity `w` (a word in the variables `X` and the constants `C`) if `w`
evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G` for the variables. -/
def SatisfiesMixedIdentity {X C : Type} (G : Type) [Group G] (c : C → G)
    (w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X → G, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c) w = 1

blocks.docstring:
A class `𝒞` of groups is a *mixed variety* if there are a set `X` of variables, a set `C`
of constant symbols and a set `W` of mixed identities (words in `X` and `C`) such that a group
belongs to `𝒞` if and only if all identities in `W` hold in it for some interpretation of the
constants.

justification.closest_existing_considered: No notion of (Birkhoff) variety of groups exists in Mathlib; searched for 'variety', 'Birkhoff', 'law'.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.2».IsMixedVariety
justification.why_needed: Anashin's notion of a mixed variety: ∃ variable set `X`, constant set `C`, set `W` of words in `X ⊕ C`, such that a group is in the class iff for some interpretation `c : C → G` all words of `W` are mixed identities of `(G, c)`.

blocks.name: IsMixedVariety
blocks.text:
/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is a *mixed variety* if there are a set `X` of variables, a set `C`
of constant symbols and a set `W` of mixed identities (words in `X` and `C`) such that a group
belongs to `𝒞` if and only if all identities in `W` hold in it for some interpretation of the
constants. -/
def IsMixedVariety (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X C : Type) (W : Set (FreeGroup (X ⊕ C))),
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒞 G ↔ ∃ c : C → G, ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w

blocks.code:
def IsClosedUnderIso (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], 𝒞 G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) → 𝒞 H
blocks.docstring: A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under isomorphism.

justification.closest_existing_considered: Inline quantification; no existing predicate for classes of groups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.2».IsClosedUnderIso
justification.why_needed: Makes explicit that the class is an abstract (isomorphism-closed) class of groups; without it Lean-specific type-level artifacts (e.g. excluding one literal type) would give trivial non-iso-closed counterexamples.

blocks.name: IsClosedUnderIso

def IsClosedUnderQuotients (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝒞 G → 𝒞 (G ⧸ N)

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib for classes of groups.

  ∀ (ι : Type) (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)], (∀ i, 𝒞 (G i)) → 𝒞 (∀ i, G i)
blocks.docstring:
A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets
(including the empty one, whose product is the trivial group).

justification.closest_existing_considered: None in Mathlib for classes of groups.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.2».IsClosedUnderPiProducts
justification.why_needed: Closure under Cartesian (unrestricted) products over an arbitrary index type `ι : Type`, including the empty product (trivial group), as required by the decomposition notes.

blocks.name: IsClosedUnderPiProducts
blocks.text:
/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets
(including the empty one, whose product is the trivial group). -/
def IsClosedUnderPiProducts (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)], (∀ i, 𝒞 (G i)) → 𝒞 (∀ i, G i)

blocks.docstring:
A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under taking those subgroups of Cartesian powers `Gⁱ` of
its members that contain the diagonal subgroup `{(g)ᵢ : g ∈ G}`, i.e. the range of
`Pi.constMonoidHom ι G`.

justification.closest_existing_considered: `Pi.constMonoidHom` (used for the diagonal); no existing closure predicate.
justification.name: Kourovka.«10.2».IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups
justification.why_needed: Closure under subgroups `H ≤ (ι → G)` of Cartesian powers of members that contain the diagonal subgroup, expressed as `(Pi.constMonoidHom ι G).range ≤ H`.

blocks.name: IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups
blocks.text:
/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under taking those subgroups of Cartesian powers `Gⁱ` of
its members that contain the diagonal subgroup `{(g)ᵢ : g ∈ G}`, i.e. the range of
`Pi.constMonoidHom ι G`. -/
def IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι G : Type) [Group G] (H : Subgroup (ι → G)),
    𝒞 G → (Pi.constMonoidHom ι G).range ≤ H → 𝒞 H

blocks.code:
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.2» :
    ∃ 𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop,
      IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderQuotients 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderPiProducts 𝒞 ∧
        IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 ∧ ¬ IsMixedVariety 𝒞 := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Construct an example of a class of groups which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed
under taking factor-groups, Cartesian products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that
contain the diagonal subgroup.

Formally: there is an (isomorphism-closed) class of groups which is closed under
factor-groups, Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup, but which is not a mixed variety.
blocks.name: kourovka.«10.2»
blocks.text:
/--
Construct an example of a class of groups which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed
under taking factor-groups, Cartesian products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that
contain the diagonal subgroup.

Formally: there is an (isomorphism-closed) class of groups which is closed under
factor-groups, Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup, but which is not a mixed variety.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.2» :
    ∃ 𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop,
      IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderQuotients 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderPiProducts 𝒞 ∧
        IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 ∧ ¬ IsMixedVariety 𝒞 := by
  sorry

/- ### Basic properties of mixed identities and mixed varieties

Every mixed variety has the four closure properties appearing in the problem, so these are
necessary conditions; the problem asks whether they are sufficient. -/

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.map {X C G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (f : G →* H)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (f ∘ c) w := by
  intro y
  choose x hx using fun v => hf (y v)
  have key : f.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c)) = FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim y (f ∘ c)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp [hx]
  simpa [hw x] using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).symm
blocks.docstring: Mixed identities are preserved by surjective homomorphisms.
blocks.name: SatisfiesMixedIdentity.map
blocks.text:
/-- Mixed identities are preserved by surjective homomorphisms. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.map {X C G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (f : G →* H)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (f ∘ c) w := by
  intro y
  choose x hx using fun v => hf (y v)
  have key : f.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c)) = FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim y (f ∘ c)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp [hx]
  simpa [hw x] using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).symm

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.subgroup {X C G : Type} [Group G] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (H : Subgroup G)
    (hc : ∀ k, c k ∈ H) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩) w := by
  intro x
  have key : H.subtype.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => (x v : G)) c) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw _)
blocks.docstring: Mixed identities pass to subgroups containing the constants.
blocks.name: SatisfiesMixedIdentity.subgroup
blocks.text:
/-- Mixed identities pass to subgroups containing the constants. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.subgroup {X C G : Type} [Group G] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (H : Subgroup G)
    (hc : ∀ k, c k ∈ H) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩) w := by
  intro x
  have key : H.subtype.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => (x v : G)) c) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw _)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.pi {X C ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    {c : ∀ i, C → G i} {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)}
    (hw : ∀ i, SatisfiesMixedIdentity (G i) (c i) w) :
    SatisfiesMixedIdentity (∀ i, G i) (fun k i => c i k) w := by
  intro x
  ext i
  have key : (Pi.evalMonoidHom G i).comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k i => c i k)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => x v i) (c i)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw i _)

    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw i _)

blocks.code:
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderIso {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro G H _ _ hG ⟨e⟩
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW H).mpr ⟨e ∘ c, fun w hw => (hc w hw).map e.toMonoidHom e.surjective⟩

theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderQuotients {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}

@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderPiProducts {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}

@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro ι G _ H hG hH
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW H).mpr ⟨fun k => ⟨Pi.constMonoidHom ι G (c k), hH ⟨c k, rfl⟩⟩, fun w hw =>
    (SatisfiesMixedIdentity.pi fun _ => hc w hw).subgroup H fun k => hH ⟨c k, rfl⟩⟩

@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isMixedVariety_isMulCommutative :
    IsMixedVariety fun G _ => IsMulCommutative G := by
  refine ⟨Bool, PEmpty,
    {⁅FreeGroup.of (Sum.inl false : Bool ⊕ PEmpty), FreeGroup.of (Sum.inl true)⁆},
    fun G _ => ⟨fun h => ⟨PEmpty.elim, ?_⟩, fun h => ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩⟩⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesMixedIdentity, map_commutatorElement,
      FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, Sum.elim_inl]
    exact fun x => commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (h.is_comm.comm _ _)
  · obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h
    have := hc _ rfl (Bool.rec a b)
    simpa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm] using this

  · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesMixedIdentity, map_commutatorElement,

claims.decomposer_note: A 'construct an example' request whose content is the existence Prop 'there is an (isomorphism-closed) class of groups closed under quotients, arbitrary unrestricted Cartesian products, and subgroups of Cartesian powers containing the diagonal subgroup, which is not a mixed variety' (i.e. the Birkhoff-type closure characterization fails); 'mixed variety' must be taken in Anashin's sense (Math. USSR Sbornik 57 (1987) 171–182: a class defined by a set of mixed identities in variables and constant symbols, a group belonging iff some interpretation of the constants makes all identities hold — matching the diagonal-subgroup closure where constants sit as constant tuples), and 'Cartesian products/powers' range over arbitrary index sets (so the empty product puts the trivial group in the class).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same mathematical content (existence of an isomorphism-closed class of groups closed under quotients, arbitrary Pi-products including the empty one, and diagonal-containing subgroups of arbitrary powers, which is not a mixed variety in Anashin's ∃-interpretation sense) and all compile with only the sorry warning. c02 was chosen as the cleanest and best documented: plain existence statement (CONTRIBUTING prefers this over answer(sorry) for non-question problems, so c06's `answer(sorry) ↔` form was not used), groups in `Type` matching the other Kourovka files (c03/c04/c05 are universe-polymorphic, which is acceptable but non-standard here), literal factor groups `G ⧸ N` plus explicit iso-closure (c07 instead uses surjective homs, equivalent), mixed identities as words in `FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)` with quantifier order ∃ interpretation of constants, ∀ word ∈ W, ∀ assignment of variables. It also includes API theorems proving that every mixed variety has all four closure properties and tests that the class of all groups and the class of abelian groups are mixed varieties, which validate the bespoke definitions. Used unchanged.
claims.source_text: Construct an example of a class of groups which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed under taking factor-groups, Cartesian products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that contain the diagonal subgroup.
claims.text_span:
Construct an example of a
class of groups which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 10.2

by V. S. Anashin

A *mixed identity* of a group $G$ is, by definition, an identity of an algebraic system
obtained from $G$ by supplementing its signature by some set of $0$-ary operations.
One can develop a theory of mixed varieties of groups on the basis of this notion
(see, for example, V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*,
Math. USSR Sbornik **57** (1987), 171–182). Construct an example of a class of groups
which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed under taking factor-groups, Cartesian
products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that contain the diagonal subgroup.

Here a mixed identity is a word $w$ in variables from a set $X$ and constant symbols from a
set $C$ (the $0$-ary operations), i.e. an element of the free group on $X \sqcup C$. A group
$G$ with an interpretation $c \colon C \to G$ of the constants satisfies $w$ if $w$ evaluates
to $1$ for all values of the variables in $G$. A class of groups is a *mixed variety* (in
Anashin's sense) if, for some set $W$ of mixed identities, it consists exactly of the groups
in which all identities of $W$ hold for some interpretation of the constants.

Every mixed variety is closed under isomorphism, factor-groups, Cartesian products (over
arbitrary index sets, so it contains the trivial group) and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup. The problem asks for a class showing that these closure
properties do not characterise mixed varieties, in contrast with Birkhoff's theorem for
ordinary varieties.

*References:*
* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
* V. S. Anashin, *Mixed identities and mixed varieties of groups*, Math. USSR Sbornik
  **57** (1987), 171–182.
-/

namespace Kourovka.«10.2»

/-- A group `G` together with an interpretation `c : C → G` of the constant symbols `C`
satisfies the mixed identity `w` (a word in the variables `X` and the constants `C`) if `w`
evaluates to `1` under every substitution of elements of `G` for the variables. -/
def SatisfiesMixedIdentity {X C : Type} (G : Type) [Group G] (c : C → G)
    (w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)) : Prop :=
  ∀ x : X → G, FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c) w = 1

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is a *mixed variety* if there are a set `X` of variables, a set `C`
of constant symbols and a set `W` of mixed identities (words in `X` and `C`) such that a group
belongs to `𝒞` if and only if all identities in `W` hold in it for some interpretation of the
constants. -/
def IsMixedVariety (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∃ (X C : Type) (W : Set (FreeGroup (X ⊕ C))),
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], 𝒞 G ↔ ∃ c : C → G, ∀ w ∈ W, SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under isomorphism. -/
def IsClosedUnderIso (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G H : Type) [Group G] [Group H], 𝒞 G → Nonempty (G ≃* H) → 𝒞 H

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under taking factor-groups. -/
def IsClosedUnderQuotients (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (G : Type) [Group G] (N : Subgroup G) [N.Normal], 𝒞 G → 𝒞 (G ⧸ N)

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets
(including the empty one, whose product is the trivial group). -/
def IsClosedUnderPiProducts (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι : Type) (G : ι → Type) [∀ i, Group (G i)], (∀ i, 𝒞 (G i)) → 𝒞 (∀ i, G i)

/-- A class `𝒞` of groups is closed under taking those subgroups of Cartesian powers `Gⁱ` of
its members that contain the diagonal subgroup `{(g)ᵢ : g ∈ G}`, i.e. the range of
`Pi.constMonoidHom ι G`. -/
def IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups (𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop) : Prop :=
  ∀ (ι G : Type) [Group G] (H : Subgroup (ι → G)),
    𝒞 G → (Pi.constMonoidHom ι G).range ≤ H → 𝒞 H

/--
Construct an example of a class of groups which is not a mixed variety, but which is closed
under taking factor-groups, Cartesian products, and those subgroups of Cartesian powers that
contain the diagonal subgroup.

Formally: there is an (isomorphism-closed) class of groups which is closed under
factor-groups, Cartesian products over arbitrary index sets and subgroups of Cartesian powers
containing the diagonal subgroup, but which is not a mixed variety.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 8 20]
theorem kourovka.«10.2» :
    ∃ 𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop,
      IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderQuotients 𝒞 ∧ IsClosedUnderPiProducts 𝒞 ∧
        IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 ∧ ¬ IsMixedVariety 𝒞 := by
  sorry

/- ### Basic properties of mixed identities and mixed varieties

Every mixed variety has the four closure properties appearing in the problem, so these are
necessary conditions; the problem asks whether they are sufficient. -/

/-- Mixed identities are preserved by surjective homomorphisms. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.map {X C G H : Type} [Group G] [Group H] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (f : G →* H)
    (hf : Function.Surjective f) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (f ∘ c) w := by
  intro y
  choose x hx using fun v => hf (y v)
  have key : f.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x c)) = FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim y (f ∘ c)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp [hx]
  simpa [hw x] using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).symm

/-- Mixed identities pass to subgroups containing the constants. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.subgroup {X C G : Type} [Group G] {c : C → G}
    {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)} (hw : SatisfiesMixedIdentity G c w) (H : Subgroup G)
    (hc : ∀ k, c k ∈ H) : SatisfiesMixedIdentity H (fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩) w := by
  intro x
  have key : H.subtype.comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k => ⟨c k, hc k⟩)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => (x v : G)) c) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw _)

/-- Mixed identities hold componentwise in Cartesian products. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem SatisfiesMixedIdentity.pi {X C ι : Type} {G : ι → Type} [∀ i, Group (G i)]
    {c : ∀ i, C → G i} {w : FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)}
    (hw : ∀ i, SatisfiesMixedIdentity (G i) (c i) w) :
    SatisfiesMixedIdentity (∀ i, G i) (fun k i => c i k) w := by
  intro x
  ext i
  have key : (Pi.evalMonoidHom G i).comp (FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim x fun k i => c i k)) =
      FreeGroup.lift (Sum.elim (fun v => x v i) (c i)) := by
    ext v
    rcases v with v | k <;> simp
  simpa using (congrArg (fun g => g w) key).trans (hw i _)

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under isomorphism. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderIso {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderIso 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro G H _ _ hG ⟨e⟩
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW H).mpr ⟨e ∘ c, fun w hw => (hc w hw).map e.toMonoidHom e.surjective⟩

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under taking factor-groups. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderQuotients {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderQuotients 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro G _ N _ hG
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW _).mpr ⟨QuotientGroup.mk' N ∘ c, fun w hw =>
    (hc w hw).map (QuotientGroup.mk' N) (QuotientGroup.mk'_surjective N)⟩

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under Cartesian products. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderPiProducts {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderPiProducts 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro ι G _ hG
  choose c hc using fun i => (hW (G i)).mp (hG i)
  exact (hW _).mpr ⟨fun k i => c i k, fun w hw => .pi fun i => hc i w hw⟩

/-- Every mixed variety is closed under those subgroups of Cartesian powers that contain the
diagonal subgroup. -/
@[category API, AMS 8 20]
theorem IsMixedVariety.isClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups {𝒞 : ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop}
    (h : IsMixedVariety 𝒞) : IsClosedUnderDiagonalSubgroups 𝒞 := by
  obtain ⟨X, C, W, hW⟩ := h
  intro ι G _ H hG hH
  obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := (hW G).mp hG
  exact (hW H).mpr ⟨fun k => ⟨Pi.constMonoidHom ι G (c k), hH ⟨c k, rfl⟩⟩, fun w hw =>
    (SatisfiesMixedIdentity.pi fun _ => hc w hw).subgroup H fun k => hH ⟨c k, rfl⟩⟩

/-- The class of all groups is a mixed variety, defined by the empty set of identities. -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isMixedVariety_all : IsMixedVariety fun _ _ => True :=
  ⟨PEmpty, PEmpty, ∅, fun G _ => by simp [SatisfiesMixedIdentity]⟩

/-- The class of abelian groups is a mixed variety, defined by the identity $[x_0, x_1] = 1$
(an ordinary identity, involving no constants). -/
@[category test, AMS 8 20]
theorem isMixedVariety_isMulCommutative :
    IsMixedVariety fun G _ => IsMulCommutative G := by
  refine ⟨Bool, PEmpty,
    {⁅FreeGroup.of (Sum.inl false : Bool ⊕ PEmpty), FreeGroup.of (Sum.inl true)⁆},
    fun G _ => ⟨fun h => ⟨PEmpty.elim, ?_⟩, fun h => ⟨⟨fun a b => ?_⟩⟩⟩⟩
  · simp only [Set.mem_singleton_iff, forall_eq, SatisfiesMixedIdentity, map_commutatorElement,
      FreeGroup.lift_apply_of, Sum.elim_inl]
    exact fun x => commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm.mpr (h.is_comm.comm _ _)
  · obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := h
    have := hc _ rfl (Bool.rec a b)
    simpa [map_commutatorElement, commutatorElement_eq_one_iff_mul_comm] using this

end Kourovka.«10.2»

items: Classes of groups are modeled as predicates `∀ (G : Type) [Group G], Prop` on groups in universe `Type` (consistent with the other Kourovka files, which quantify over `G : Type`); index sets, variable sets and constant sets also live in `Type`.

Isomorphism-closure is stated as a separate explicit condition (implicit in 'class of groups'); together with closure under `G ⧸ N` it is equivalent to closure under surjective homomorphic images (factor-groups in the abstract sense). This is needed to rule out Lean-specific non-iso-closed trivial counterexamples.

'Mixed variety' follows Anashin's sense as described in the decomposition notes: a group belongs iff SOME interpretation of the constant symbols (uniform over all identities in `W`) makes all identities hold; the variable set `X` and constant set `C` are arbitrary types (an arbitrary `X` is equivalent to a countable one since each word uses finitely many generators). Mixed identities `u = v` are encoded as single words `u v⁻¹` in `FreeGroup (X ⊕ C)`.

Cartesian products range over arbitrary index types including the empty one, so any class satisfying the closure conditions contains the trivial group (as every mixed variety does); this prevents the empty class from being a trivial counterexample.
'Construct an example' is rendered as a plain existence theorem (no `answer(sorry)`), as it is not a yes/no question.

API lemmas (with short proofs) verify that every mixed variety has the four closure properties, and tests show the class of all groups and the class of abelian groups are mixed varieties; these serve as sanity checks of the definitions.

reviewer_notes: Reading fixed per decomposition notes: 'mixed variety' = class of groups G for which SOME interpretation φ : C → G of a fixed set C of constant symbols makes every word of a fixed set W ⊆ FreeGroup (X ⊕ C) evaluate to 1 under all assignments of the variables. Using an arbitrary variable type X is equivalent to countably many variables since every word is finite and groups are nonempty; recording identities as w = 1 rather than u = v is equivalent in groups. Cartesian products/powers range over all index types in `Type` (ZFC-set analogue), including the empty one, so every closed class contains the trivial group and the empty class is not a spurious witness; the class of trivial groups and the class of all groups are mixed varieties, so they are not witnesses either. Isomorphism-closure is imposed explicitly (implicit in 'class of groups'; every mixed variety is iso-closed) to rule out Lean-artefact predicates that are not invariant under isomorphism. Residual uncertainty is only about whether Anashin's paper (not available in the sandbox) defines mixed varieties exactly in this ∃-interpretation sense; the decomposition notes fix this reading and it is the only one under which the three closure operators in the problem are the natural necessary conditions.
